title: Postman collection export: variable reference in an auth attribute entry
summary: The same synthetic Postman Collection v2.1 export as the literal twin, with one change: the entry whose key is value now holds the double-brace reference {{postman_api_key}} instead of a credential-shaped string. The header name, the in entry and the collection id are unchanged.
rationale: Postman's documentation recommends exactly this arrangement for API key and bearer auth: store the value in a variable and reference it by name. The twin differs from the literal in one value only, so the expectation flips on that value. A reader that reacts to the apikey auth block, to the entry label value or to the name postman_api_key reports a reference that holds no secret byte and penalises the recommended practice. The reference names a variable that is not defined in this input; where it resolves is outside the bytes.

expectation.rationale: No span. Postman documents the double-brace form as a reference to a variable, not as a value, and recommends storing API key and bearer values in variables and referencing them. The string {{postman_api_key}} therefore carries no credential bytes. Preconditions: the input is read as exported text; no variable resolution is performed, so the expectation says nothing about what the name resolves to in any other input.

sources.supports: For API key auth: 'You can store your values in variables for extra security.' For bearer auth: 'For added security, store it in a variable and reference the variable by name.'
Double curly braces reference a variable throughout Postman, for example in a request's authorization settings.
sources.locator: section: Use variables, 'double curly braces ({{ and }})'

sources.supports: A variable is referred to from anywhere in the collection using the double-brace {{variable-id}} format and replaced by its value when resolved.
Request auth can use environment, collection and global variables, and Postman recommends storing sensitive data as vault secrets.

relations.note: One property changed: the value of the value attribute entry, a literal for a reference. Expected outcome flips from must-flag to must-not-flag.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04; no scanner was run. Origin: evidence-derived twin of the literal case, synthetic input. This case adds the Postman auth attribute layout to the generic reference rule; it does not restate that a reference is safe.
